feature: A transition on the timeline reads as a transition
summary: A transition on a cut is now the mock's band: a cyan to orange bar with a white edge, the transition icon in the middle and a grip at each end, and solid, so the clip's name no longer shows through it. The second piece's name starts just past the band instead of under it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open a screen recording, put the playhead at 0:02 and press Command K.
Click the clip, click the cut, and pick Cross dissolve in the picker that opens at the cut.
Zoom the timeline right in and look at the band across the cut.
Switch the Mac to Light appearance and look again.
Click the band, then drag either end grip to make it longer.
Right-click the band and look at the cut's menu.
Change the Type to Dip to black and look at the dashed outline.

evaluate: At the default zoom, can you tell at a glance which cuts carry a transition?
Is the band's icon readable on both ends of the gradient, in light and in dark?
Zoomed right in, does the wide band still read as one transition, or does its grey middle look washed out?
With the join's own grip gone from under the band, do you miss being able to drag the cut there, or is Roll Edit to Playhead on the band's right-click enough?
rough: The band matches the mock's colour: the mock's 75% gradient is drawn over the same dark the mock's timeline has behind it, so it looks the same over any clip and nothing under it shows through.
Zoomed right in, the middle of the cyan to orange gradient is a muted grey-brown over a long stretch. It matches the mock's gradient, just drawn wide.

The join's own trim grip is no longer drawn through a band. The band picks the cut and right-clicking it opens the cut's menu, but dragging the band does not roll the edit; Roll Edit to Playhead in that menu does.
A dip's white icon sits right where the playhead usually is after you apply it, so the playhead line covers it until you move.
